# SParC: Cross-Domain Semantic Parsing in Context

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#sparc)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/P19-1443.pdf) · ACL 2019 proceedings, pages 4511-4523

**Reading coverage:** All thirteen PDF pages, Sections 1-7 and Appendices A.1-A.2; Tables 1-9, contextual analyses and example sequences/figure captions covered.

## Research question

Follow-up database questions omit or replace prior constraints and entities, requiring semantic interpretation across turns and unseen schemas.

## Method

Fifteen SQL-experienced students construct thematically related sequences around Spider interaction goals, annotate each turn with SQL, and undergo multi-stage review. Baselines extend sequence-to-sequence and syntax-tree parsers with question history.

## Evaluation

The corpus has 4,298 sequences and 12,726 questions on 200 databases, split into disjoint train/development/test databases. Question match requires exact set matching of SQL clauses; interaction match requires every turn to match.

## What the results support

Context improves both baselines, but best test question match is 20.2%; whole-interaction scores remain below 10%. Performance declines across later turns, where queries also tend to be structurally harder.

## Limits and qualifications

These are expert-authored, goal-guided question sequences, not a live user simulator or clarification-policy evaluation. Exact set match follows a preferred annotation pattern and is not general semantic equivalence. Analyses of thematic relations use only 102 examples; the rare answer-refinement category has fewer than ten.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A foundational dataset for context retention and evolving requests, complementary to explicit ambiguity and answerability benchmarks.
